children: Rocket Lab (RKLB) and Viasat (VSAT) shares were in focus on Wednesday after Viasat successfully launched its Maxwell spacecraft on Tuesday for a NASA communications demonstration.

The mission is part of Viasat’s work under two NASA Communications Services Project contract awards totaling $81 million. Rocket Lab built the spacecraft, which flew aboard SpaceX’s Bandwagon-5 rideshare mission.
This is Viasat’s second demonstration under NASA’s Communications Services Project. Its first demonstration involved relaying launch telemetry during Blue Origin’s New Glenn launch in November 2025.

“Yesterday’s launch represents the culmination of years of innovation, engineering and collaboration across Viasat, NASA and our industry partners,” said John Reeves, vice president of Space and Mission Systems at Viasat Government.

What Will Viasat Test?
Viasat will conduct on-orbit tests and demonstrations over five months, through March 2027, to demonstrate its satellite communications services for low Earth orbit (LEO) missions.

The demonstrations will test Viasat’s Ka- and L-band relay services, which are designed to support low-latency communications for spacecraft in LEO. The company will also test direct-to-ground communications through its Real-Time Earth Ground-Station-as-a-Service platform, which supports S-, X- and Ka-band communications.

The work is part of NASA’s Communications Services Project, which is evaluating commercial satellite communications services as the agency prepares to retire its Tracking and Data Relay Satellite fleet.
What Is Rocket Lab’s Role?

Rocket Lab built the Maxwell spacecraft at its Long Beach facility, incorporating in-house components and subsystems including solar panels, reaction wheels, star trackers, and flight and ground software. The spacecraft provides power, communications, propulsion and attitude control for the demonstration.
Rocket Lab also supplied an L-band radio to support tests of telemetry, tracking and command communications through Viasat’s L-band network.
How Retail Views RKLB, VSAT and SPCX

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment toward VSAT remained in ‘bearish’ territory over the past 24 hours, with message volume at ‘high’ levels. Sentiment toward RKLB stayed ‘bullish’, while message volume also remained ‘high’.

Meanwhile, retail sentiment toward SPCX climbed to ‘extremely bullish’, accompanied by ‘extremely high’ message volume over the past 24 hours. SPCX was also among Stocktwits’ trending tickers at the time of writing.
One user on Stocktwits warned of an impending selloff, predicting that RKLB shares would close below $50.
